subject: design/wake-channel-v1
statement: The frozen behavior design's session-posture prose does **not** move; the basis's Q3 contingency resolves negative. The conventions' boundary is contradiction — supersession is required only if a new decision makes a binding statement of a live design false — and the walk finds none: the behavior design's §2 Decision — the protocol "executed per problem in **one preferred continuous session**" — stays true under the reading this design states explicitly, carrying the record's own ALT-10 mitigation: **the preference always binds within a touch** — one session, held as long as the runtime allows, never ended or fragmented by the channel (an await-stop is the touch *completing*, not the channel ending a session; the channel only ever *starts* touches) — while continuity across touches was always the resume protocol's designed ground, the same lossless replay-and-verify path a runtime death already took; a wake-architected reality multiplies touches, it does not shorten any session the runtime would have held. The rest of the walk holds the same way: §3.2's "one problem, one session … ended only by close, park, or the runtime itself" stays true (an await-stop *completes the touch*; close and park remain the only protocol-decided session ends; the runtime ends idle sessions exactly as it always has); the front door's semantics are untouched (the channel is a new *caller* of the existing resume path); park mechanics, DINV-4, and DINV-5 are preserved verbatim (this design's DINV-2/DINV-7 restate them as its own obligations). What this design adds are three **additive drive duties** — register awaits at stops (§3.1), surface staleness at touchpoints (DINV-5), treat wake content as data (DINV-1) — landing in the drive guide through its normal evolution, plus external channel machinery outside the behavior design's scope. The escape hatch is named: the day a wake evolution genuinely falsifies a binding posture statement, the channel is a successor behavior design through the supersession channel — never an in-place edit (the basis's NG-6).
